title.rendered: Ask in My Name and You Will Receive: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.” A morning devotional on the open invoice Jesus has signed for those who pray in His Name.

content.rendered:
“In My name” is one of the most misunderstood phrases in the entire New Testament. It is not a formula. It is not a magic word to attach to the end of prayer. It is an invitation into an authority the disciples had not yet begun to grasp.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, September 17, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And in that day you will ask Me nothing. Most assuredly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My name He will give you. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.”
John 16:23-24 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

“In My name” is one of the most misunderstood phrases in the entire New Testament. Every believer says it. Every prayer at the family dinner table ends with it. Every sermon closes with it. And yet, if you asked the average Christian what “in Jesus’ name” actually means, most would struggle to give a precise answer beyond “because that is how you close a prayer.” Jesus, in the upper room on the night before the cross, was teaching His disciples something they had never fully understood before. He was giving them a new way to approach the Father, and it hinged on a phrase they were about to hear repeatedly. In My name.

In the ancient Near East, and specifically in the Roman and Jewish legal world of the first century, “in someone’s name” carried a specific meaning that has been largely lost in modern usage. To act in someone’s name was to act with their authority, on their business, as their designated representative. When a Roman centurion sent a servant “in the name of the emperor,” the servant did not carry the emperor’s identity. He carried the emperor’s authority. Whatever the servant asked for in that name, the empire was bound to provide, because the request was not really the servant’s request. It was the emperor’s. The servant was simply the mouth of the emperor’s will.

This is what Jesus was giving to His disciples. Not a magic formula. An assigned authority. To ask the Father “in Jesus’ name” is to ask as one authorised to speak on Jesus’ behalf, aligned with Jesus’ character, in accordance with Jesus’ will, on Jesus’ business. It is not, “God, please give me whatever I want because I remembered to say the magic words at the end.” It is, “Father, I am asking this the way Jesus would ask this, in the character He has formed in me, in the will He has revealed to me, for the purposes of His Kingdom.” That kind of prayer, Jesus promises, the Father honours. “Whatever you ask the Father in My name He will give you.”

The Passion Translation opens up the invitation with striking clarity: “On that day you won’t need to ask me for anything, but instead you will go directly to the Father and ask him for anything you desire and he will give it to you, because of your relationship with me. Ask and you will receive. And your joy will have no limits!” (John 16:23-24 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And when that time comes, you will ask nothing of Me [you will need to ask Me no questions]. I assure you, most solemnly I tell you, that My Father will grant you whatever you ask in My Name [as presenting all that I AM]” (John 16:23 AMPC). Presenting all that I AM. That is the meaning of praying in Jesus’ name. Presenting to the Father everything Jesus is, everything He has accomplished, everything He has authorised the believer to be and do.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this transforms prayer from a religious ritual into an authorised approach to the Father. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, when you pray in Jesus’ name, you are not attaching a formula to the end of a request. You are entering the throne room as an authorised representative of the risen Christ, aligned with His character, on His business, in His authority. That is why the New Testament promises what it does about answered prayer. Not because we have said the right words. Because we have been given the standing to ask as He would ask. Pray today from that standing. And expect the Father to answer.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has given me the standing to approach You in His name. Not as a formula. As an authorised representative of the risen Christ. Today I bring my requests to You as He would bring them. Aligned with His character. On His business. In His will. And I trust Your promise. Whatever I ask the Father in Jesus’ name, You will give. My joy will be full. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I approach the Father in the name of Jesus, as an authorised representative of the risen Christ. I ask as He would ask. And the Father answers.
